heading: INT. CURLING CLUB - ICE SHEET - NIGHT

units.text: INT. CURLING CLUB - ICE SHEET - NIGHT
A century-old curling hall, the ice scarred with the day's stones.
Brass trophies sweat behind glass.
Under the hanging lamps, three figures stand at the hog line, all of them very still.
COACH ABIGAIL STRAND (60s, tweed cap, a face lined like old paper) holds a broom across her chest like a rifle.
Her skip, DESMOND "DES" ACHEAMPONG (30s, club jacket, one glove missing), crouches behind the final stone.
And across the ice, the opposing lead, LUCIE FONTAINE-ARCHAMBAULT (20s, borrowed sweater too large), waits with her broom raised, her knuckles white around the handle.
Draw weight, Des. Nothing more.
units.name: ABIGAIL

units.text: Coach, if I miss--
units.name: DES

units.text: Take your time. We have all night.
units.name: LUCIE

units.text: Nobody asked you, girl.
units.name: ABIGAIL

units.text: She's just being polite.
units.name: DES

units.text: I'm not being anything.
units.name: LUCIE

units.text: Des settles into the hack.
He rolls the stone, and it glides, turning slowly, toward the button.
Abigail sweeps without being asked.
Lucie lowers her broom and does not sweep.
The stone slows and slows, and stops.
A hush.
A single point of ice crystal falls from a lamp.
Des remains crouched, still staring at the stone.
Abigail puts her broom down on the ice and walks across to Lucie.
She straightens the girl's collar, and says nothing.
Lucie nods once and extends her hand.
Des finally stands, and shakes it.
